# [TASK] Implement User Service

## Task
User Service: registration and login, JWT access tokens with rotating refresh
tokens, Spring Security, profile management, and favorites/watchlist stored in
PostgreSQL behind Flyway migrations.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Registration and login work end to end against a real PostgreSQL schema,
      passwords are BCrypt-hashed, and a duplicate username is rejected
      (`UserServiceIntegrationTest.register`,
      `UserServiceIntegrationTest.registerDuplicateRejected`,
      `AuthServiceTest.registerHashesPasswordAndIssuesTokens`)
- [x] An access token carries the `sub`/`userId`/`roles` claims the gateway
      reads, and a tampered, wrongly signed or expired token is rejected on
      both sides (`JwtTokenProviderTest`, `JwtUtilTest` in api-gateway)
- [x] Refresh rotates the token and kills the old one; logout revokes every
      refresh token the user holds
      (`UserServiceIntegrationTest.refreshRotation`,
      `UserServiceIntegrationTest.logoutRevokesRefreshTokens`)
- [x] Profile, password change, favorites and watchlist work behind the token,
      adds and removes are idempotent, and lists come back newest first
      (`UserServiceIntegrationTest.profileRequiresToken`,
      `UserServiceIntegrationTest.favoritesRoundTrip`,
      `UserServiceIntegrationTest.watchlistRoundTrip`,
      `UserServiceIntegrationTest.passwordChange`)
- [x] Health probes, the OpenAPI document and Swagger UI are served without a
      token, the service registers with Eureka, and line coverage stays at or
      above 80% (`PrometheusEndpointTest.healthProbesRespond`,
      `OpenApiDocsTest`, the newman request "Eureka Registry (core services
      registered)", `./gradlew :backend:user-service:jacocoTestCoverageVerification`)

## Estimate
**Hours:** 10-12

## Notes
Coverage was written here as 85%. The gate the build enforces is 80%, set in
#108, so the criterion states 80%.

Role-based access control is infrastructure only: the JWT `roles` claim
becomes Spring Security authorities and `@EnableMethodSecurity` is on, but no
endpoint restricts by role because there is no admin-only function in this
service to gate.

Refresh tokens are opaque values stored as a SHA-256 hash, rotated on every
use. An access token stays valid until it expires, including after logout.

MapStruct is not used; the service layer builds the response records directly.
